WindowsCraft 0.15.38 (screens, in-game monitors, gaming monitors and tablets for Cobbleverse)

New in 0.15.38: own copies of apps no longer reach your desk. Only what you open at a monitor (its
taskbar, Start menu or desktop) can be its own copy, and only if you switched that app on; your
desk's apps and everything they open stay as they are. Anything else you open there (games,
launchers, apps left off) runs normally, on that monitor.

New in 0.15.37: the screen-capture helper rebuilt the clean way (nothing of the PC it was built on inside).

New in 0.15.36: own copies of apps work as before, but only for the apps you switch on. A page of
its own (U → "Own copies of apps") lists every app on your PC with its own switch, all off to
start. An app switched on starts as each monitor's own copy (its own sound and sign-ins); games
and everything else always run normally.

New in 0.15.33: in-game monitors don't affect each other. Turning one on or off leaves the
others as they were (their size, windows and sound), a new one starts empty, and turning one
off closes its apps. No more slow capture for hours after a monitor came on.

New in 0.15.32: apps run normally on in-game monitors again (games, Steam, Roblox, Minecraft,
Store apps); a monitor's own copies are off unless you turn them on.

New in 0.15.31: your desk's windows stay on your desk when in-game monitors come and go, and
closing the game never closes or hides them.

New in 0.15.30: a browser on a monitor (Chrome, Edge, Brave and the like) starts signed in
like the one on your desk.

New in 0.15.29: own copies work again: what you start on a monitor is its own copy, with its
own sound. The monitor's corners have no holes.

New in 0.15.28: set up each monitor's own copies (Like your desk, Its own PC, Leaves no trace);
joined monitors share them, and one set up differently stops being joined.

New in 0.15.27: name your screens (Rename, in a screen's menu); a screen is remembered by its name
and settings, never by what was on it. Settings → Menu size makes the menu bigger or smaller.

New in 0.15.26: a monitor's own copies start signed in like your desk every time ("Logins
follow my desk"), and what you save there goes to your own Desktop, Documents and Downloads.

New in 0.15.25: Sandboxie's own window and messages no longer pop up.

New in 0.15.24: "own copies" really work now — each monitor's apps get their own logins and
sound (Sandboxie's settings were never saved on a PC without administrator rights).

New in 0.15.23: a friend's clicks on your monitors count as held in more apps; turning on a new
monitor no longer takes an app's sound from the monitor it plays on.

New in 0.15.22: every app you start at a monitor is its own copy there (Discord and launchers
too), apps show their real names, and a gaming monitor's picture sits behind its frame.

New in 0.15.21: leaving with several monitors on turns them all off at once, and each takes its
own apps with it. A monitor no longer goes dark because Sandboxie was slow.

New in 0.15.20: clicking an app that has windows on two monitors moves its sound between their
walls without it ever blaring from your speakers in between.

New in 0.15.19: in-game monitors run at your screen's refresh rate (144 Hz on a 144/165 Hz
screen), so their apps feel as quick as on your desk. A monitor's taskbar is never cut in half.
Sitting at a monitor, looking around, zooming and looking straight again are Ctrl+Alt (+ mouse,
+ scroll, + Space): plain Alt is your apps'.

New in 0.15.18: changing a monitor's resolution no longer turns every monitor off, and a
monitor keeps the size you picked.

New in 0.15.17: opening another copy of an app on a monitor no longer shuts the in-game
monitors down.

New in 0.15.16: someone sitting at your monitor without moving no longer wakes the video's
time bar or flickers your hovers. A viewer whose PC can't keep up gets 720p at 30 pictures a
second, not an ever blurrier picture.

New in 0.15.15: a monitor's sound stays on its wall, also from Store apps like Media Player and
while monitors are being added. Screens you watch cost your PC much less (the nearest plays full,
the others lighter; at most 1080 lines). "Shader pack on screens" is now one setting for everyone
on the server, on by default.

New in 0.15.14: an app with a window on an in-game monitor is heard only from the wall, also
when you click its window on your own desktop. Apps you open while sitting at a monitor (Steam…)
open on it, and one that opened on a monitor (Roblox…) stays there when it comes to the front. On joined monitors, the mouse goes across again
after you've dragged a window over.

New in 0.15.13: with "You hear it from the wall too" on, the sound you share no longer loses
little bits now and then on a busy PC (the helper that captures it checks the app's volume on a
thread of its own now), so a film sounds whole for you and your friends.

New in 0.15.12: sound and picture line up. Friends heard a shared screen's sound about a
seventh of a second after the picture (your PC stamped it late, and their game never waited for
it); now they come together, also for a friend 100 ms away whose line goes up and down. Sound the
capture loses for a moment (a busy PC, while it turns the app down for you) is filled with an
equal bit of silence instead of making everything after it run early.

New in 0.15.11: watching someone far away (about 100 ms, going up and down) no longer smears
the picture: when a piece of it is lost on the way, the screen holds its last picture for a
moment instead (at most a second; the sound goes on), and lost pieces are waited for a little
longer, so it happens much less (on a simulated bad line: 35 smeared pictures in 40 s before,
none now, and smoother too). A window you share no longer freezes while you or a friend use it.
Screens sit flush on their blocks, and a gaming monitor's picture now fills its whole screen
(16:9) instead of leaving dark bars beside it.

New in 0.15.10: WindowsCraft keeps to its own monitors. It no longer changes how Windows starts
Task Manager (that affected your desk too), friends' controllers work only at your in-game
monitors (not at a window of your desk you share), and games WindowsCraft starts on an in-game
monitor can take a friend's controller even while you play Minecraft in front (SDL games ignore
it by default); the same game on your desk isn't changed.

New in 0.15.9: friends can play controller games on your screens while you play Minecraft. When
someone you allowed sits at one of your screens with a game controller, it shows up on your PC as
an Xbox controller of their own, for any game that supports controllers (also when that game isn't
the window in front). Needs ViGEmBus on the PC sharing the screen (Nefarius' virtual gamepad
driver; WindowsCraft doesn't install it). Measured on one PC: a button press reaches the game in
about 2 ms, plus your friend's internet delay.

New in 0.15.8: sitting down at a monitor puts the cursor where you were pointing and keeps it
on that monitor, also on a busy PC (the game could let go of the cursor late and leave it at the
monitor's edge, free to slip off). The Windows self-test now saves its report on the desktop you
actually see (with OneDrive, that's a different folder) and checks the monitor's picture too.

New in 0.15.7: windows you share on a wall (not just in-game monitors) now also use direct GPU
sharing with Sodium; with 0.15.6 they could still fall back to copying through the CPU. While
nobody is watching a screen you share, your PC no longer keeps making full-size copies of it for
a stream that's paused. Resizing a window you share no longer makes your wall flicker to an
older picture for a moment. Servers with a server-ip set open WindowsCraft's relay on that
address only.

New in 0.15.6: direct GPU sharing now works with Sodium. Sodium's "no error" OpenGL mode (on by
default) hid a mistake that made the shared pictures come out black, so WindowsCraft turned GPU
sharing off and copied every picture through the CPU instead. Measured with a 4K in-game monitor
in the Cobbleverse modpack (Iris + Solas): the game went from 37 to 89 frames a second, the
monitor from 22 to 52 pictures a second, and the picture's delay from ~100 ms to a few ms. If
your PC had decided "black" before, it tests again by itself.

New in 0.15.5: when someone you allowed uses one of your in-game monitors, their clicks and keys
reach it the moment they arrive, instead of waiting for your game to draw its next frame (measured:
a click took about 21 ms to reach the app with your game at 30 frames a second; now about 3 ms),
and finding the window under their click never makes your game stutter. And when someone's screen
had a hiccup in its sound, the extra sound kept to bridge the next one (and with it the picture,
which waits for the sound) is given back once things have been steady for a couple of minutes.

New in 0.15.4: fixes 0.15.3 restarting the stream of a screen you share every few seconds while
your own wall of it looked small (the people watching saw it pause and fall behind). Sitting down
at one of your screens brings its full-size picture back at once. The Windows self-test no longer
opens Task Manager on PCs where Windows starts it as administrator (it then stayed in front and
spoiled the tests after it).

New in 0.15.3: Settings -> Performance is Automatic (WindowsCraft decides, and says what it's
doing right now) or Advanced (pick each setting yourself); settings you had turned off stay off.
Each of your screens can have its own picks on its Picture page. New and on by Automatic: your
own walls get a smaller copy of a big screen while it looks small from where you are (a 4K
in-game monitor across the room was copied in full 20 times a second; now it keeps up and the
game runs smoother). Full size as you come closer or sit down; what others see never changes.

New in 0.15.2: someone else's screen shows each change the moment it arrives (the last change
before a screen went still could wait for the next one), its pictures are coloured by the
graphics card (less work for the PC watching), and a movie on it plays with its sound in step
while you just watch (the picture takes the quickest way again the moment you use the screen).
WindowsCraft now uses one tested FFmpeg version (fetched once more in the background if yours is
older), and direct GPU sharing double-checks before it decides it doesn't work on your PC.

New in 0.15.1: the sound of a screen you share now reaches the people watching (on Windows most
of it was lost on the way); someone who starts watching gets the full frame rate (they were
dropped to 30 a second by mistake); your own walls get each picture sooner, and the people
watching see your screen about a third sooner (more on a screen that changes slowly); a screen you aren't
looking at no longer costs your PC the work of its picture (its sound keeps playing). And
"/windowscraft measure start 60" measures for a minute what your screens cost and how long each
step takes (off unless you start it; the report lands in windowscraft/measurements).

1. Close Minecraft.
2. Right-click this zip and choose "Extract All...", then open the extracted folder.
3. Double-click "Install WindowsCraft.bat".
   If Windows says "Windows protected your PC": click "More info", then "Run anyway".
4. Start Cobbleverse and join the server as usual.

The server needs this version too: put the same windowscraft .jar into the server's "mods"
folder (delete the old windowscraft .jar there) and restart it. Anyone already on 0.14.2 or
newer is offered this update in chat when they join, and it updates itself (anyone older than
0.14.2 installs it by hand once, like this).

U anywhere: the WindowsCraft menu - all your screens (what's open on them, who can use them,
their size and picture) and the settings.
In-game monitor: look at a black concrete wall or a gaming monitor block and press U (the first
time it offers to install a free display driver). Press O to sit down and use it with your real
mouse and keyboard - it's then shown flat and sharp on your screen like a real monitor, as big
as fits in what you see of the game (never under your taskbar), with the room around it (Alt +
scroll out: still sharp, just smaller); Esc gets up.
Hold Alt and look at your monitor to point and click on it without sitting down.
An app that only runs once (Discord, Calculator...) already open on your desk: opening it from a
monitor brings it over, in the middle of that monitor (and opening it from your own taskbar brings
it back). Each monitor plays only its own sound, never mixed: U on a monitor -> "Own copies of apps" -> Set up
(free Sandboxie-Plus, installed hidden; Windows asks once). Then every app you start at that monitor
is its own copy: its own sound, its own logins (sign in once there, it stays). Your desk's apps are
never touched; Discord and WhatsApp come over instead. Full-screen videos stay full screen when you
press Esc. U again turns it off; sneak + U opens its menu.
Gaming monitors and tablets: creative tab "WindowsCraft" (or craft them). A gaming monitor faces
you when placed (8 directions). Placed right beside, above or below another one it joins it (no
stand, edge to edge, turned to face you - stand at your seat while placing; sneak to keep it flat)
- joined monitors are joined in Windows too, so windows drag across them.
Each screen's volume (0-500 %): U menu, the slider under its name.
A tablet: holding it turns it on; right-click holds it up (it fills your screen), Esc puts it
down (it keeps playing in your hand), sneak + right-click turns it off.
To share a window or your screen instead: sneak + U on a wall, pick one, Go Live.
On someone else's screen, U opens listening options (3D or direct sound, volume, mute).
Press O while looking at a live screen for theater mode.

If U does nothing or in-game monitors won't turn on: the display driver got stuck. WindowsCraft
now notices that and offers "Repair driver" (Windows asks for permission). Restarting the PC
fixes it too.
If something else about in-game monitors misbehaves: close Minecraft, open the "Windows self-test"
folder and double-click "Run self-test.bat". It takes a couple of minutes (your screens blink and
the mouse moves - leave the PC alone meanwhile) and puts "WindowsCraft self-test" on your desktop:
send that folder's report.
